title: IMPRESS-A: the API and the loop

acts.name: Functionality
acts.question: what can you write against this that you cannot write against a pipeline?
acts.gap: every toolkit that exists is one of the four real stages of a single chain, plus mocks, and nobody outside this package has authored either a toolkit or a policy

acts.name: Performance
acts.question: what does the loop cost, and where does it serialise?
acts.gap: no concurrent run and no serial baseline anywhere in the deck, so nothing divides into a speedup - and the stages were mocks, so this times the ENGINE and never the science

acts.name: Usability
acts.question: application, platform, or component?
acts.gap: nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign; the live four-hour run on 21-22 is the reference pipeline's toolkit with an LLM on it, NOT this engine - and `--model C` with no caller falls back to model D after 5 s instead of failing

orders.name: A · full
orders.fits: a 40-minute slot, or a working session where questions land inline

orders.name: B · default
orders.fits: a 35-minute slot: drops the loop/driver slide, the intent seam, the task-agent phases, the signature finding and the layering test. Each is recoverable in a sentence, and 5 still carries the map

orders.name: C · hard twenty
orders.fits: a hard 20 that leaves room for discussion: the framing, the three dividers, one surface per act, the measured run, the interlock finding, the live evidence from next door, status and asks

orders.name: D · for users
orders.fits: a room that will RUN this rather than write against it: the framing, what a tool and a refusal are, the measured run, then the four user-directed slides (19-22) and the asks. No protocols, no layering, no type lattice

protect: **Protect 2, 3, 12, 15, 16, 17, 21, 22, 26 and 27.** Two and three are what buy the rest of the deck (the caveats at minute two and the named weak dimension); 12, 15 and 17 are the only slides carrying evidence from a run this deck performed; 16 is what keeps the performance act honest; 21 and 22 carry the only evidence from real hardware and the only transcribed figures, so their red caveats travel with them or they do not travel at all; 26 is status and 27 is the asks. Never cut a divider - a cut deck without them is a list of slides. Backups B1 (compute patterns) and B2 (the type lattice) are out of every order; do not put them back to fill time.
say_out_loud: that nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign, so the component claim is empty and the control plane is the most carefully built unused thing in here; that the four-hour comparison on slide 21 is the REFERENCE pipeline's toolkit driven by an LLM - different code, no campaign engine, no gates, no interlock - so it is evidence about the idea and not about this engine; that its reference arm came in about 2x worse than its own record, so the 3.3x is an upper bound and nobody should quote it; that `replicas > 1` DOES run - the mock campaign in this deck ran two lineages - and what has never run is `replicas > 1` on the real six-stage chain (backlog A10); and that every stage in the measured run was a mock, so the timings are the engine and never the science.
